title: Cross-Platform Frequency Cap Dispute with Conflicting Analytics Sources
question: Mindshare is demanding a credit for frequency cap violation. What is the correct operational determination?

contributor.name: Natasha Williams
contributor.title: Ad Operations Director
contributor.domain_expertise: Programmatic deal reconciliation, advertiser entity management, IO interpretation, cross-platform attribution, make-good decisions

choices: A credit is owed for the full overlap segment (34% of households) based on Amplitude's 6.8x figure, calculated against the combined IO value of $520K

A partial credit is owed only after validating the actual overlap exposure using LiveRamp's deterministic match — Amplitude's 6.8x estimate and Mindshare's '30%+' claim are both probabilistic and neither is contractually authoritative
No credit is owed because the trafficker's Feb 8 note proves cross-platform dedup was technically impossible, making the IO frequency language unenforceable as a performance guarantee
No credit is owed — each platform individually honored the 5x cap, and the IO was structured as two separate orders (0087 and 0088) making each independently compliant
